starting_principles: Second kinematic equation s(t) = ut + 0.5 a t^2
assumptions: n is a positive integer second

ordered_steps.action_description: Define displacement in the n-th second as difference between total displacement at t = n and t = n-1
ordered_steps.justification: Physical definition of displacement over the interval [n-1, n].

ordered_steps.action_description: Substitute second kinematic equation for t = n and t = n - 1
ordered_steps.justification: Evaluation of position function at specific integer endpoints.

ordered_steps.action_description: Subtract the two displacement expressions and expand algebraically
ordered_steps.equation_latex: s_n = \left( u n + \frac{1}{2} a n^2 \right) - \left( u n - u + \frac{1}{2} a (n^2 - 2 n + 1) \right)
s_n = u + \frac{1}{2} a \left( n^2 - n^2 + 2 n - 1 \right) = u + \frac{a}{2} (2 n - 1)

applicability_conditions: Assumes duration of interval is strictly Delta t = 1 s
source_references: Concepts of Physics Vol 1 by H.C. Verma (Chapter 3, p. 49)
